stem: Who was the first one to propose a model for the structure of an atom ?
expl: The first person to propose a model for the structure of the atom was J. J. Thomson. In 1898, he proposed the plum pudding model. This model has been given different names, for example—plum pudding model, raisin pudding model, or watermelon model. In this model, the positive charge of the atom is considered like a pudding or a watermelon, in which electrons are present like plums or seeds. An important feature of this model is that the mass of the atom is assumed to be uniformly distributed throughout the atom. Although this model explained the electrical neutrality of the atom, it was not found consistent with the results of later experiments.

stem:
Dalton’s atomic theory successfully explained
(i) Law of conservation of mass.
(ii) Law of constant composition.
(iii) Law of radioactivity.
(iv) Law of multiple proportions.
expl: 1. John Dalton presented the atomic theory in 1803, in which he gave important facts about the nature of matter. According to Dalton’s atomic theory, matter is made up of indivisible particles called atoms. 2. All atoms of an element are identical in size, mass, and chemical properties. 3. Atoms of different elements are different from each other. 4. In chemical reactions, atoms only get rearranged. 5. In compounds, atoms of different elements combine in simple whole-number ratios. 6. Dalton’s atomic theory successfully explained the law of conservation of mass, the law of constant composition (definite proportions), and the law of multiple proportions. Law of conservation of mass – According to the law of conservation of mass, matter can neither be created nor destroyed. Law of definite proportions – This law was given by the French chemist Joseph Proust. According to him, in a compound, the ratio of masses of the elements is always constant. Law of multiple proportions – The law of multiple proportions was given by Dalton in 1803. According to this law, if two elements combine to form more than one compound, then the masses of one element that combine with a fixed mass of the other element are in the ratio of small whole numbers. Therefore, option (c) is the correct answer.

stem: The positively charged part at the centre of an atom is called as :

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The positively charged part at the centre of an atom is called the nucleus. The nucleus is the central core of the atom. In the nucleus, protons and neutrons are present and are called nucleons. A proton is a positively charged particle, and a neutron is neutral; therefore, the nucleus is positively charged. The mass of protons and neutrons (approximately the same) is 1.67 × 10-27 kg, and their discoveries are attributed to E. Goldstein and James Chadwick, respectively.
